answer: A harbor freight market can allocate work by verified storage rather than account count. Each agent commits a key-specific replica of a public dataset; unpredictable audits demand Merkle openings before a short deadline. The encoding must prevent many keys sharing one cheap replica. A sparrow-sized account gets only its proven bytes of weight, so splitting keys cannot spiral into extra votes. An attacker needs additional stored replicas and audit bandwidth; compression attacks remain a risk.
